seo.title: SQL Server client for {devices}
seo.description: Run T-SQL scripts with GO batches and PRINT output, sign in with a SQL login, Kerberos or Microsoft Entra ID, and back up SQL Server to .bacpac.

header.title: SQL Server client
header.lead: Run T-SQL scripts with GO batches and PRINT output, and sign in with a SQL Server login, Kerberos or Microsoft Entra ID.

bands.title: Connect
text: Enter a host and TCP port, then choose <ui>Authentication</ui>: SQL Server login, Kerberos or Microsoft Entra ID. Database-scoped logins, Azure SQL contained users included, also need the Database field.

Kerberos uses the ticket in your credential cache, or requests one from a principal and password you enter; connect by hostname, because the ticket is issued for the server’s registered SPN. <cloudAuth>Microsoft Entra ID</cloudAuth> uses device-code sign-in with your Azure application’s client ID.
New connections start on Preferred, which on SQL Server encrypts the login only. Choose Required or stricter to encrypt the whole session.

bands.title: Scripts, batches and edits
text: Scripts split at GO lines, and GO 5 repeats the batch before it five times. Each result set opens in its own tab, PRINT output and messages show in Output, and execution stops at the first failed batch with its editor line in the error. Use BEGIN TRAN and COMMIT when batches must be transactional.

Sessions open with ANSI_NULLS and QUOTED_IDENTIFIER on, as filtered indexes and indexed views require, so compare with IS NULL rather than = NULL. ⌘K changes database without reconnecting, and new rows leave IDENTITY columns to the server.

bands.title: Schema
text: The Structure tab stages changes to columns, indexes, foreign keys and constraints as T-SQL, and a schema can be dropped from the sidebar once it holds no objects. Compare & Sync ({compareSyncTier}) compares SQL Server schemas or data and separates its statements with GO for sqlcmd or SQL Server Management Studio.

bands.title: Monitor and back up
text: The <dashboard>Server Dashboard</dashboard> shows sessions, uptime, database size and the queries running longer than a second, and ends a session with <ui>Terminate Session</ui>. There is no Cancel Query on SQL Server.

Backup Dump writes a .bacpac with {dumpTool}, which you download from Microsoft, and Restore Dump loads one into an empty database. SqlPackage takes a password only on its command line, so TablePro asks before it starts; Windows or Entra authentication passes none.

moveData: Import {importFormats} files, SQL files with their GO batches. Export tables or results as {exportFormats}; SQL exports use GO separators too.
iphone: Sign in with a SQL Server login, browse tables as cards, edit rows that have a primary key and run T-SQL in the Query tab. A connection that uses Microsoft Entra ID comes from your Mac, and you sign in to Microsoft when you open it.

faq.question: Does TablePro work with Azure SQL Database?
faq.answer: Yes. Use yourserver.database.windows.net as the host, set SSL to Required or stricter, and sign in with a SQL login or Microsoft Entra ID. A contained user also needs the Database field.

faq.question: Why does a script say “Must declare the scalar variable”?
faq.answer: The statement that reads the variable ran in a different batch from its DECLARE: a GO line sits between them, or ⌘⏎ ran only the statement at the cursor. Run both together.

faq.question: Do I need FreeTDS or an ODBC driver?
faq.answer: No. The driver carries its own FreeTDS, so nothing else is installed and your freetds.conf is not read. Only Backup Dump and Restore Dump need a tool of your own: {dumpTool}.

otherTools.text: SQL Server Management Studio covers administration beyond TablePro, such as SQL Server Agent jobs, Always On availability groups and performance tuning, and Microsoft has retired Azure Data Studio; see <ssms>TablePro vs SQL Server Management Studio</ssms>.
